content: Is this an oversight or is there a good reason for this?

I guess the question is why you want a universe polymorphic FVarIdMap in the first place. I don't think there's any particular reason why you'd want it to not be universe polymorphic, except that none of the other metaprogramming stuff is universe polymorphic anyways so there is not much point.
This is especially true since MetaM : Type -> Type which sets a hard boundary on what values you can pass around in a metaprogramming context (i.e. values whose type lives in the type universe Type).

I think this leads to an argument along the lines of

  • I want FVarIdMap to be polymorphic. Why would you want that if MetaM isn't
  • I want MetaM to be polymorphic. Why would you want that if IO isn't
  • I want IO to be universe polymorphic. Why would you want that if IO.println isn't
  • I want IO.println to be polymorphic. This isnt something the FRO wants to spend time on
It's very hard to provide a compelling example (in the form of actual code) of a motivation for universe polymorphism if you have to make many patches to lean itself to even attempt to compile it
(though a fairly simple abstract example is when implementing dynamic pointers via a dependent triple of a type, a typeclass, and a member of that type)
